## Reference behavior exercised

The complete unchanged reference `ModelVersionsTest.checkSupportsParallelSync` maps to the one selected Rust test. All nine original AGP literals, outcomes, order and named diagnostic assertions remain:

The executed supplemental tests cover the surrounding preview/micro edges, every valid `7.3.0-alpha00` through `alpha99` spelling, signed producer override ordering and descriptions, missing/not-applicable capabilities, malformed and unknown explicit AGP facts, historical preview padding, signed-Int component limits and bounded invalid input. The eligible alpha00 edge follows the pinned literal closed/open ranges; it is not a guessed exception. Invalid explicit AGP remains an error even with a newer producer, so a consumer cannot mistake an unproved capability for verified eligibility.

Production `supports_parallel_sync` matches pinned `BasicModules.ModelFeature.SUPPORTS_PARALLEL_SYNC`: producer >= (8, 0), or AGP in [7.2.0, 7.3.0-alpha01), or AGP >= 7.3.0-alpha04. The separate Rust AGP comparison preserves Alpha < Beta < Rc < Dev < Stable and the pinned numeric/padding grammar. Minimum-consumer compatibility and producer descriptions do not influence this feature's eligibility, matching the original helper and comparator. Available false, absent capability, not-applicable capability, malformed facts and unsupported qualifiers remain distinguishable typed outcomes.

No production caller or scheduler was added: a search of `crates` finds the API definition and test calls only. The API mutates no settings, project or sync state, and initiates no Gradle request. Therefore this change introduces no current shortcut, focus, loading, cancellation or concurrency workflow to claim as validated. Future scheduling controllers must add their own compatibility, settings, lifecycle and UI gates; the pure eligibility result does not establish those behaviors.
